title: JavaScript essentials
targetPerformance: After 20 focused hours, solve at least 18 of 22 JavaScript tasks in 35 minutes, including array transformations, immutable object updates, a closure, sequential and concurrent Promise flows, and a small class-based build.
whyItMatters: A compact command of JavaScript's core data and control patterns lets you turn a problem into a tested function before framework details get in the way.

subskills.title: Bindings and value types
subskills.why: Choose stable bindings and recognize the runtime type you actually have.
subskills.selfCorrection: Ask whether the name or the value needs to change, then test null, undefined, and an empty value separately.
drills: Repair a function that changes a binding unnecessarily.

subskills.title: Transform arrays
subskills.why: Map, filter, and reduce express common data pipelines clearly and testably.
subskills.selfCorrection: Write the input and output shape first; check the empty array and verify whether the callback returns a value.
drills: Map numbers without mutating the input.
Filter by a boundary that includes or excludes zero.
Reduce an empty and a mixed-sign array.

subskills.title: Compose objects and destructure safely
subskills.why: Object spread and destructuring make data boundaries explicit while preserving immutability.
subskills.selfCorrection: Check which properties are copied, which are renamed, and whether a nested input is absent before reading it.
drills: Pick a subset of fields without mutating the source.
Merge a patch while keeping unrelated fields.

subskills.title: Use closures for private state
subskills.why: A closure keeps a small piece of state next to the functions that intentionally change it.
subskills.selfCorrection: Name the variable captured by the returned function and test two independent factory calls.
drills: Return a multiplier that remembers a factor.
Keep an accumulator private across calls.

subskills.title: Compose asynchronous results
subskills.why: Promises and async/await let you sequence or combine work without hidden timing assumptions.
subskills.selfCorrection: Separate a value from a Promise of that value; use await only where ordering matters and test rejection explicitly.
drills: Return a resolved value from an async function.
Run task functions in input order.
Summarize fulfilled and rejected Promise results.

subskills.title: Model behavior with classes
subskills.why: A small class can make state, invariants, and related methods easy to discover at the call site.
subskills.selfCorrection: Check constructor defaults, `this` at each call site, and whether one instance leaks state into another.
drills: Create an instance with a default field.
Add methods that preserve an invariant.
Build a small class-backed task board.

resources.title: MDN JavaScript Guide
resources.why: Review the language's core syntax and control patterns from a maintained reference.

resources.title: MDN Array reference
resources.why: Check callback contracts and edge cases for map, filter, and reduce.

resources.title: MDN Promise reference
resources.why: Check Promise composition, allSettled, and async function behavior.

resources.title: MDN Classes reference
resources.why: Review constructors, methods, and instance state.

barriers.barrier: The language surface feels too broad
barriers.fix: Use one pure function at a time and defer framework APIs until the six subskills feel routine.

barriers.barrier: A failing test feels like a dead end
barriers.fix: Read the first failing assertion, write the smallest counterexample, and retry with one changed assumption.

barriers.barrier: Async code seems to require real services
barriers.fix: Practice with deterministic Promise-returning functions; no network, timers, or external packages are needed.

barriers.barrier: I copy patterns without knowing the data shape
barriers.fix: State the input and output shape in a sentence before writing the function body.
